title: Cost of the low-degree estimator
statement:
Let $n,k$ be natural numbers, let $\varepsilon$ be a positive learning parameter, and let the target be a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube. Every outcome in the support of the low-degree Fourier estimator's output law has cost
\[\bigl(R,0,R+R(n+1)\bigr),\qquad R=\text{the low-degree learner's random-example cost for }(n,k,\varepsilon).\]
hypotheses_covered: the target is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube
the outcome belongs to the support of the estimator's run-with-cost law
